questions.question: Describe the summer rainfall pattern and where it is found.
questions.expected_answer: Most of South Africa, including Gauteng, Limpopo, Mpumalanga, North West, the Free State and KwaZulu-Natal, gets most of its rain in summer, from about October to March, mostly in afternoon thunderstorms when the land heats up and warm, moist air rises. Winters are dry and sunny with cold nights. A bar graph shows tall bars in summer months.

questions.question: Explain why Cape Town gets rain in winter.
questions.expected_answer: In winter, cold fronts move in from the Atlantic Ocean one after another. When a cold front arrives, the wind gets strong, the temperature drops and rain falls. Summers in the south-western Cape are hot and dry. A bar graph for Cape Town shows tall bars in May to August.

questions.question: How can you tell the three rainfall patterns apart on bar graphs?
questions.expected_answer: Check the title, then find the tallest bars. If they are in the summer months, around October to March, it is summer rainfall. If they are in the winter months, around May to August, it is winter rainfall. If the bars are fairly even in all months, it is all-year rainfall, as at George.
